presentation.line1: 🎙️ « Welcome to UNIT – an explosive strategic card game where each player builds armies to trigger... a Revolution. »
presentation.line2: 🎙️ « With a simple deck of 54 cards, you assemble unit columns – from Ace to 10 – to attack, defend, and manipulate the battlefield. »
presentation.line3: 🎙️ « Beware: special cards like Kings, Jacks, or Jokers can turn everything around. »
presentation.line4: 🎙️ « The goal? Reduce your opponent's health to zero... or trigger a Revolution that deals 10 damage in one blow. »
presentation.line5: 🎙️ « Simple to understand, deep to master... and every game is unique. »
presentation.line6: 🎙️ « Ready to change the course of History? It's time to enter UNIT. »

debut-partie.title: Game Start
content: Each player starts with a personal deck of 54 cards.
They draw 7 cards at the beginning of the game.
From these 7 cards, 2 cards of their choice are placed face down in reserve, on the board.
The player keeps 5 cards in hand, and 2 cards in reserve.
debut-partie.highlight: 🧠 Important reminder: The reserve is a strategic extension of the hand, it remains face down and accessible during the game.

structure-tour.title: Turn Structure
content: Every turn always follows the same sequence.

cas-1.title: Case 1: The player starts their turn with 7 cards
cas-1.subtitle: (5 in hand + 2 in reserve)
content: Mandatory discard: The player must discard 1 card from their hand (they choose which).
Draw: Then, they draw 1 card to return to a total of 7 cards.
Action phase: They can then:
• Place cards to build units,
• Use a special card (Jack, King, etc.),
• Attack or activate an effect.
End of turn: Once their actions are done, the player announces the end of their turn.
cas-1.warning: 🛑 If the player cannot or does not want to perform any action, they must still announce the end of their turn.

cas-2.title: Case 2: The player has fewer than 7 cards at the start of their turn
cas-2.subtitle: (because they played cards previously)
content: The player immediately draws the number of cards needed to return to 7 cards (hand + reserve).
Then they enter the action phase: they can play, attack, activate an effect...
End of turn: they end their turn as usual.

rappel-general.title: General Reminder
content: Players can never exceed 7 cards (5 in hand + 2 in reserve).
If at 7 at the start of a turn: must discard 1 card before drawing.
If they played cards: they draw directly, without discarding.
Each turn, a player can act or pass, but must indicate it.

introduction-phase.title: The Action Phase
content: During their turn, after drawing, the player enters their action phase.
They can perform several types of actions, in the order they wish, as long as they respect the following limits:

actions-disponibles.title: Available actions
content: Each action costs 1 action, except in special cases.
Here is the list of main actions a player can perform during their turn:

action-construire.title: 1. Play a card to build a unit
content: The player places a card in the corresponding column (by suit).
Units must be placed in ascending order, from Ace to 10.
action-construire.highlight: ➡️ ✅ This action allows progress toward an attack or a Revolution.

action-speciale.title: 2. Play a special card (Jack, King, Queen)
content: The player can summon a special card by:
• Sacrifice (cards already placed),
• Using a Joker,
• Or a Lucky 7.
The summon counts as an action.
action-speciale.highlight: 💡 Exception: If a Jack is summoned by Joker or sacrifice, it can attack immediately in the same turn. (Otherwise, it is passive until the next turn.)

action-attaquer.title: 3. Attack with a unit
content: A unit can attack only once in its category.
This attack costs 1 action.
action-attaquer.warning: ⚠️ After an attack, the entire unit category is deactivated, even if the attack is blocked.

action-echanger.title: 4. Exchange a card with a placed Joker
content: If a Joker is placed on the board to replace a card, the player can replace it with the real card (same suit and value).
The Joker returns to the hand or reserve depending on its origin.
action-echanger.highlight: ➡️ ✅ This exchange counts as an action.

defense.title: 5. Defense during the opponent's turn
content: Although defense does not occur during the player's action phase, it is important to know.
A player can block an opponent's attack:
• If they have a JOKER (in hand or reserve) → they play it immediately, it blocks the attack.
• If a Lucky 7 is present in the attacked column, in the right position (after the 6), then:
- It blocks a single attack.
- It is then deactivated until the column is destroyed and rebuilt.
defense.highlight: 🧠 Remember: A Joker can block any attack (except Revolution). Each defense is valid once, then the card goes to the graveyard or becomes inactive.

limites-action.title: Action Limits
content: The player can perform as many actions as they wish during their turn, as long as they have cards to do so.
However:
• They can only make one Joker exchange per turn.
• They can only attack once per unit category.
• Some cards (Jack) do not attack immediately, except in special cases.

fin-tour.title: End of Turn
content: Once all actions are done, the player announces the end of their turn.
If they take no action, they must still declare the end of their turn.

introduction-activateurs.title: Activators: Lucky 7 & Joker
content: In UNIT, to build a unit column, it is not enough to place cards in order. You must activate the column with a special card called an activator.
There are two types of activators:
• 🟦 The Lucky 7
• 🃏 The Joker

comment-activer.title: How to activate a column?
content: To start a column, you must place an Ace, then build up progressively to the 6.
This activator is placed in a special area of the column, called the reserveSuitColumn.
comment-activer.highlight: 🧠 But to go beyond the 6 (and play the 8, 9, 10), it is mandatory to have an activator in place.

fonctionnement-activateur.title: How an activator works
content: When a Lucky 7 or Joker is played as an activator:
• It is placed next to the column, in the reserveSuitColumn.
• It unlocks the progression toward 8, 9, 10.
• It remains active as long as the column is not destroyed.

exemple-activation.title: Example
content: You have cards from Ace to 6 in Diamonds.
You place a Lucky 7 of Diamonds in the reserveSuitColumn.
You can now place the 8, 9, 10 of Diamonds.

conditions-importantes.title: Watch out for conditions!
content: A Joker or any Lucky 7 can be played at the start of the game to open play, even if it doesn't match the suit.
conditions-importantes.highlight: ✅ This allows you to advance and adapt your strategy.
conditions-importantes.warning: ❌ But to go from the 6 to 8 in a column, you must have the correct Lucky 7 of the same suit as the column.

echange-activateur.title: The activator exchange
content: If you placed the wrong 7 or a Joker in the reserveSuitColumn, don't panic:
• You can exchange the activator for the correct Lucky 7 of the column's suit if you draw it into your hand or reserve.
• The previous Joker or 7 returns to its original position.
• This exchange costs one action.
• It allows unlocking the progression toward the top of the column (and possibly preparing a Revolution).

attaque-activateur.title: What happens in case of attack?
content: If a Jack attacks a column activated with a 7 or a Joker:
• All cards in the column, including the activator, go to the graveyard.
• This cancels the column's progress.
• You'll have to start again from the Ace.

activateurs-cartes-speciales.title: Activators and special cards (Face cards)
content: Lucky 7s and Jokers can also be used to summon face cards:
• King → 7 or Joker → Graveyard
• Queen → 7 or Joker → Graveyard
• Jack → 7 or Joker → Graveyard
activateurs-cartes-speciales.warning: ❗ As soon as a 7 or Joker is used to play a special card, it is immediately sent to the graveyard.

resume-activateurs.title: Key Takeaways
content: ▶️ Activate a column = Ace + 7 or Joker in the reserveSuitColumn.
🔒 To place an 8, you need the Lucky 7 of the same suit.
🔁 You can exchange the activator if needed (single action).
💥 In case of Jack attack, the column + activator are destroyed.
👑 Activators can also be used to play a King, Queen or Jack, but they then go to the graveyard.

revolution-intro.title: The Revolution – The Ultimate Attack
content: The Revolution is the supreme strategic goal in UNIT.
It is the most powerful attack in the game, one that can turn an entire game around if well prepared.
It symbolizes the perfect completion of a full column and the flawless execution of a plan.

revolution-conditions.title: Mandatory conditions to trigger a Revolution
content: To launch a Revolution, all these conditions must be met:
✅ Have placed all 10 cards of the same suit in order, from Ace to 10
✅ Have not used a Joker in the column (no replacement)
✅ Have correctly activated the column with the right Lucky 7 of the suit
✅ Have placed the 10 (this automatically triggers the Revolution)

revolution-effects.title: Immediate effects of the Revolution
content: 💥 The opponent's King of the same suit is destroyed, even if still in play.
💥 The opponent takes 10 direct damage, with no possible defense.
🪦 The entire column (Ace to 10) is sent to the graveyard after the attack.
❗ No Joker, Lucky 7, Jack or other effect can block a Revolution.

revolution-unstoppable.title: Why the Revolution is unstoppable
content: The Revolution is the only totally unstoppable attack in the game.
It ignores all defense mechanisms:
✅ Ignores Kings
✅ Ignores Jokers
✅ Ignores Lucky 7s
✅ Ignores reserve cards
✅ Ignores any counter action
It represents a rare but devastating event that rewards patient and rigorous players.

revolution-joker-case.title: Special case: Joker in the column
content: If a single Joker replaces a card in the column:
❌ The Revolution is blocked.
The column is considered incomplete, even if it appears visually complete.
You'll need to exchange the Joker for the real card (with an action) to unlock the Revolution.

revolution-strategy.title: Strategic reflection
content: The Joker is a useful but dangerous card to place in a column if you're aiming for the Revolution.
Sometimes it's better to delay an action than to sacrifice the possibility of a Revolution.
Keeping the column pure guarantees a brutal and spectacular outcome.

revolution-perfect.title: The Perfect Revolution
content: A perfect Revolution occurs when the player triggers a Revolution without having performed any other attack with their units during the game.
🎖️ It demonstrates absolute tempo control, patience, and a pure style of play.
It can surprise an overly aggressive opponent and eliminate them in a single strike.

revolution-summary.title: Quick Summary
content: 🎯 Required cards: Ace to 10, same suit, no Joker
🔧 Mandatory activation: Yes, with matching Lucky 7
⚡ Trigger: Place the 10
💥 Effects: King destruction + 10 direct damage
🛡️ Blockable?: No, impossible
🪦 Consequences: Entire column sent to graveyard
🏆 Strategic bonus: Perfect Revolution if no other attack made

defense-intro.title: Defense – Protecting Your Life Points and Units
content: In UNIT, defense is just as important as attack.
Certain cards and positions allow you to cancel or limit the impact of an opponent's action.

defense-objectives.title: Objective of defense
content: Prevent the opponent:
• From dealing direct damage to your life points.
• From destroying your units or special cards too easily.
• From breaking your strategy (e.g.: preventing a Jack from clearing a column).

joker-defense.title: The Joker – Universal Defender
content: 🔹 Effect: The Joker can block any attack, regardless of the column or the attacking card.
🔹 Limit: It cannot block a Revolution.
📋 Usage:
• Played from hand or reserve during the opponent's turn.
• After use, it immediately goes to the graveyard.
💡 Tip: Keeping a Joker in hand is often safer than using it for attack.

seven-defense.title: The Lucky 7 – Column Shield
content: 🔹 Effect: A Lucky 7 placed in a column, in its normal position (after the 6), can block a single attack targeting that column.
📋 Conditions:
• The 7 must be the same suit as the column.
• It only protects the column where it is placed.
⚡ After use:
• The 7 is deactivated until the column is destroyed and rebuilt.
• It remains physically in play, but no longer blocks.
💡 Tip: A well-positioned 7 can force the opponent to waste an attack or Joker.

defense-interactions.title: Important interactions
content: 🔸 Classic unit (1–6): Blocked by Joker ✅ | Blocked by Lucky 7 ✅
🔸 8 or 9: Blocked by Joker ✅ | Blocked by Lucky 7 ✅
🔸 Jack: Blocked by Joker ✅ | Blocked by Lucky 7 ✅
🔸 King: Blocked by Joker ❌ | Blocked by Lucky 7 ❌
🔸 Joker: Blocked by Joker ✅ | Blocked by Lucky 7 ✅
🔸 Revolution (10): Blocked by Joker ❌ | Blocked by Lucky 7 ❌

defense-strategy.title: Defensive strategy
content: 🎯 Anticipate: Keep at least one active defense option each turn.
🎯 Protect key columns: Place a Lucky 7 on the most advanced column.
🎯 Force opponent choices: Make a column look vulnerable while it's protected.
🎯 Manage resources: A Joker used too early can cost you the game.

defense-summary.title: Quick Summary
content: 🃏 Joker = universal defense against everything except Revolution.
7️⃣ Lucky 7 = local defense on its column.
🚫 No card blocks the Revolution.

melange-intro.title: Strategic Shuffle – Rebuilding Your Deck
content: In UNIT, it is sometimes necessary to shuffle the graveyard cards back into the deck to continue playing.
This action, called a strategic shuffle, can be used to recover key cards or to avoid getting stuck.

quand-melanger.title: When to do a strategic shuffle?
content: A strategic shuffle can be performed before any other action on your turn when:
• You want to reintroduce important cards into your deck.
• You are stuck in your progress.
• Your deck is not yet empty but you want to reset the distribution.

regles-melange.title: Rules of the strategic shuffle
content: 📅 Timing:
• Must be done at the start of your turn, before discarding or drawing.
🔄 Procedure:
• You discard all cards from your hand.
• The 2 reserve cards remain in place.
• You shuffle your deck and graveyard to form a new deck.
🥇 First time:
• During the first strategic shuffle of the game, you can play normally after the shuffle.
🔁 Subsequent times:
• All strategic shuffles after the first force you to skip your turn after the shuffle (no action possible).

limitations-melange.title: Limitations after subsequent shuffles
content: If you do a strategic shuffle after the first:
❌ You cannot attack that turn.
❌ You cannot use a Joker to defend on the next opponent's turn.
✅ A Lucky 7 already active on the board retains its defense.

cas-particuliers.title: Special cases
content: 🗂️ Empty deck:
• If your deck is empty when you need to draw, you automatically shuffle the graveyard back into the deck, without losing your turn.
• This case is not considered a strategic shuffle.
⚠️ Risky strategy:
• Multiplying strategic shuffles increases randomness and can delay your plans.
• Better to keep this option as an occasional tool, not a habit.

astuce-strategique.title: Strategic tip
content: The strategic shuffle is a double-edged weapon:
✅ It can unlock a situation…
❌ …but it often costs you tempo.
💡 Use it with a clear objective, not out of habit.
astuce-strategique.highlight: 🎯 Tip: Plan your strategic shuffle around specific cards you want to recover, not just to 'see what happens'.

sacrifice-intro.title: Sacrifice – Playing a Face Card
content: In UNIT, to play certain special cards called face cards (King, Queen, Jack), you can use the sacrifice mechanic.
This action consists of removing cards already placed on the board to pay the summoning cost.

principe-sacrifice.title: Principle of sacrifice
content: 🎯 Objective: Remove a certain number of cards from the board to summon a face card.
🪦 Destination: Sacrificed cards go to the graveyard after use.
📏 Key rule: Always start with the highest card in each chosen column.

cartes-non-sacrifiables.title: Cards that cannot be sacrificed
content: ❌ Ace
❌ Lucky 7 placed in the column
❌ 10 of Revolution
❌ Any card located under an Ace, a placed 7 or a 10: these cards are blocked and cannot be sacrificed.

regles-selection.title: Selection rules
content: 🔝 Always start with the highest card in a column.
• Example: if the highest card in Spades is a 6♠, you can sacrifice it.
🔄 Complete with other highest cards from other columns if needed.
• Example: 6♠ + 8♥ + 2♦ for a King.
🌈 Mixing suits is allowed as long as each chosen card is the highest in its column.
⛓️ Chain sacrifice in a column:
• You can go down from the highest toward the bottom as long as no blocking card is encountered.
• Example: 6♠, 5♠, 4♠ in the same column.

couts-invocation.title: Summoning costs by sacrifice
content: 👑 King: 3 cards
👸 Queen: 2 cards
🃏 Jack: 1 card (8 or 9 only)

attaque-immediate-valet.title: Special case – Immediate Jack attack
content: If a Jack is summoned by:
• Sacrifice
• Or Joker
➡️ It can attack immediately in the same turn.
(Otherwise, it becomes passive and can only attack next turn.)

astuce-sacrifice.title: Strategic tip
content: Sacrifice is a strong tactical choice:
❌ You lose cards already placed...
✅ ...but you gain a key piece.
💡 Use it to break an opponent's tempo or surprise with an immediate effect.
astuce-sacrifice.highlight: ⚔️ Sacrifice transforms your present resources into immediate power. Timing is crucial!

roi-intro.title: The King – Supreme Shield
content: The King is the ultimate defensive piece in UNIT.
When in play, it fully protects your life points against attacks from units of the same suit, and forces the opponent to find a specific response.

effet-roi.title: Effect of the King
content: As long as a King is present for a given suit:
🛡️ No unit of that suit below 8 can attack your life points.
🛡️ These units also cannot destroy the King.
Only certain attacks can bypass the King:
⚔️ 8 or 9 of the same suit → beat the King and destroy it.
🃏 Joker → destroys a King of any suit.
💥 Revolution (10) → destroys the King and deals 10 direct damage.

conditions-roi.title: Conditions for playing a King
content: Three possible methods:
⚔️ Sacrifice:
• Sacrifice 3 cards, each being the highest in their column (excluding Ace, 7, 10).
🃏 Joker:
• Play a Joker, which then goes to the graveyard.
7️⃣ Lucky 7:
• Play a Lucky 7, which then goes to the graveyard.

positionnement-roi.title: Positioning
content: 👑 The King is placed on the 'King' slot of its suit on the board.
🔒 Once placed, it remains until destroyed by a valid attack.

perte-roi.title: Loss of the King
content: If the King is beaten by an 8, 9, Joker or Revolution:
🪦 It is immediately sent to the graveyard.
❌ The protection it provided disappears instantly.

strategie-roi.title: Strategy with the King
content: 🛡️ Defensive: Block an advanced opponent suit to gain time.
⏰ Temporary: Force the opponent to waste an 8, 9 or Joker to clear the way.
🚧 Preventive: Playing a King early can stifle an entire opponent category.

resume-roi.title: Key Takeaways
content: The King doesn't win the game, but it can prevent the opponent from taking it.
Well played, it becomes a true wall in the opponent's tempo.
resume-roi.highlight: 👑 The King transforms passive defense into active board control. A strategic placement can change the course of a game!

dame-intro.title: The Queen – Ladies First
content: The Queen is the only completely unattackable card in UNIT.
She can never be destroyed nor prevented from carrying out her effect.
Her main role: heal your life points.

immunite-dame.title: Absolute immunity
content: The Queen can never be attacked by any card or effect:
✅ Immune to the Joker
✅ Immune to the Jack
✅ Immune to classic units
Her effect triggers no matter what.

effet-soin.title: Main effect – Healing
content: Depending on the method used to play her, the Queen immediately heals:
⚔️ Sacrifice (2 cards, each the highest in their column):
• +2 HP → Queen goes to graveyard
7️⃣ Played with a Lucky 7:
• +2 HP → Queen and 7 go to graveyard
🃏 Played with a Joker:
• +4 HP → Queen and Joker go to graveyard

defi-dame.title: Special case – Queen Challenge (Joker only)
content: When the Queen is played with a Joker, the player can launch the Queen Challenge:
🎭 The Queen is placed face down (Hearts, Diamonds, Clubs or Spades).
🤔 The opponent must guess her suit.
Result:
❌ Wrong answer → +5 HP for the player who launched the challenge.
✅ Right answer → +1 HP for the player who launched the challenge.
➡️ Regardless of the outcome, the Queen and Joker go to the graveyard after the challenge.

regles-pose-dame.title: Placement rules
content: Three methods:
⚔️ Sacrifice: 2 highest column cards (excluding Ace, 7, 10) → +2 HP.
7️⃣ Lucky 7: placed in graveyard after use → +2 HP.
🃏 Joker: placed in graveyard after use → +4 HP or Queen Challenge.

strategie-dame.title: Strategy with the Queen
content: 🔒 Safety: No risk of losing the Queen before she acts.
💊 Support: Ideal for recovering HP at a critical moment.
🎭 Psychological pressure: With the Queen Challenge, you force the opponent to guess, creating tension.

resume-dame.title: Key Takeaways
content: The Queen is the ultimate healing card in UNIT, protected by the Ladies First status.
Well used, she can reverse a game in a single action.
resume-dame.highlight: 👸 The Queen combines absolute safety with recovery potential. The Queen Challenge adds a unique psychological dimension to the game!

valet-intro.title: The Jack – The Elimination Weapon
content: The Jack is an offensive card in UNIT.
It is one of the most powerful ways to destroy opponent columns and apply pressure, but at a cost: it is always sacrificed after use.

role-valet.title: Main role
content: The Jack is a specialized attacker:
⚔️ It can destroy an opponent unit of the same suit.
💥 Against small units, it can sweep an entire column.
🪦 However, it is consumed as soon as it attacks.

invocation-valet.title: Jack summon
content: Three ways to put it into play:
⚔️ Sacrifice:
• Sacrifice an 8 or 9 (highest card in a column)
• State: Active immediately
🃏 Joker:
• Play a Joker (which goes to graveyard)
• State: Active immediately
7️⃣ Lucky 7:
• Play a Lucky 7 (which goes to graveyard)
• State: Placed passive → attack available only next turn

cycle-fonctionnement.title: Operating cycle
content: ⚡ Active:
• Can immediately attack an opponent unit of the same suit.
• After its attack, the Jack is sent to the graveyard.
😴 Passive:
• If played via a Lucky 7, the Jack cannot attack this turn.
• It becomes active at the start of the next turn.

cibles-autorisees.title: Allowed targets
content: The Jack can attack:
✅ A unit of value ≤ 6 → the entire opponent column is destroyed (column sent to graveyard + Jack to graveyard).
⚠️ A unit of 8 or 9 → direct combat, result depending on rules (risk of losing the Jack).
The Jack cannot attack:
❌ A Queen (protected by Ladies First).
❌ A King.
❌ Another Joker.

exemples-actions.title: Action examples
content: 🎯 Active Jack → attacks a 5♠ → the entire opponent Spades column is destroyed, Jack also goes to graveyard.
⚠️ Active Jack → attacks an 8♥ → risky combat, Jack can be countered.
⚠️ Active Jack → attacks a 9♦ → same, possible counter.

strategie-valet.title: Strategy with the Jack
content: 💥 Disruption weapon: destroy an advanced opponent column to break their tempo.
⚖️ Calculated sacrifice: losing a Jack to force the opponent to rebuild an entire column can be worth it.
⚡ Immediate combo: summoning a Jack via a Joker or sacrifice allows immediate attack and surprises the opponent.
⏰ Timing: waiting until the opponent has invested heavily in a column before destroying it maximizes the Jack's value.

resume-valet.title: Key Takeaways
content: The Jack is a double-edged sword: it destroys, but destroys itself with.
Well played, it can turn a game around in a single action.
resume-valet.highlight: 🗡️ The Jack embodies tactical sacrifice: lose to win better. Its timing can determine the outcome of a game!

joker-intro.title: The Joker – The Legendary Card
content: The Joker is the most powerful and versatile card in UNIT.
It is a unique card, capable of intervening in almost all phases of the game: attack, defense, activation, healing, or even temporary replacement.
But beware: each Joker use is single-use and always has an important consequence.

roles-joker.title: The Joker's roles
content: The Joker can be used in 5 main ways:
⚔️ Attack (destroy units or face cards)
🛡️ Defend (block an attack)
🔄 Replace (temporarily hold the place of a missing card)
💊 Heal (+3 life points)
🔧 Activate a column or face card (like a Lucky 7)

utilisation-offensive.title: Offensive use – Attack
content: The Joker can destroy any unit in an opponent column, even if it's not the highest.
Effects:
• The destroyed card goes to the graveyard.
• All cards above become unusable until the column is rebuilt.
Example: if a Joker destroys a 6♣, then the 7♣, 8♣, 9♣ and 10♣ cannot be played until the chain is repaired.
The Joker can also:
✅ Destroy a King (regardless of suit)
✅ Destroy a Jack (regardless of suit)
🚫 Limits:
❌ Cannot attack an Ace
❌ Cannot attack a Lucky 7
❌ Cannot attack a Revolution 10

utilisation-defensive.title: Defensive use – Blocking
content: The Joker can be played from hand or reserve during the opponent's turn.
✅ Effect: it blocks any attack (unit, Jack, opponent Joker, etc.).
🚫 Only exception: it cannot block a Revolution.
After use, it goes to the graveyard.

utilisation-remplacement.title: Use as replacement (substitution)
content: The Joker can be placed on the board to temporarily replace a missing card in a column.
This allows continuing to build the column without waiting for the real card.
⚠️ Important consequences:
While the Joker replaces a card:
• The corresponding unit category is deactivated (cannot attack anymore).
• Example: a Joker replaces a 4♠ → the 4–5–6♠ category cannot attack.
• Category units are protected: they cannot be destroyed by an opponent's Jack or Joker.
• A Revolution is impossible if a Joker is present in the column.
📌 Exchange possible:
• The player can exchange the Joker for the real card (if they draw it).
• The Joker then returns to hand or reserve.
• This exchange counts as an action.

utilisation-soin.title: Healing use
content: Played directly from hand or reserve, the Joker can:
💊 Immediately restore +3 life points to the player.
🪦 After use, it goes to the graveyard.

utilisation-activateur.title: Use as activator
content: The Joker can replace a Lucky 7 as a column activator.
It can therefore be placed in the reserveSuitColumn to allow passing from 6 to 8.
It can also be sacrificed to summon a King, Queen, or Jack, exactly like a 7.
⚠️ Warning: a Joker used this way is immediately sent to the graveyard.

interaction-speciale.title: Special interaction – Joker vs Lucky 7
content: If a Joker attacks a unit in a column where a Lucky 7 is active, then:
🛡️ The attack is blocked by the 7.
🪦 The Joker is sent to the graveyard.
😴 The 7 is then deactivated (it remains placed but no longer protects).

strategie-joker.title: Strategy with the Joker
content: 🔄 Polymorphic: it can do everything, but each choice is final.
🛡️ Defensive weapon: often more profitable used as a block than for attack.
🚫 Revolution blocker: placing a Joker in a column advances you… but blocks access to the Revolution.
💎 Rare resource: each Joker is precious, better to use it at a key moment.

resume-joker.title: Quick Summary
content: 📊 Usage → Main Effect → Limit:
⚔️ Attack → Destroys King, Jack or unit → Not Ace, 7, 10
🛡️ Defense → Blocks any attack → Not Revolution
🔄 Replacement → Replaces missing card → Deactivates category / blocks Revolution
💊 Healing → +3 HP immediately → Single use
🔧 Activator → Replaces 7 for column or face card → Goes to graveyard

conclusion-joker.title: Key Takeaways
content: The Joker is the most flexible and dangerous card in UNIT.
Poorly used, it can block your own strategies (especially the Revolution).
Well used, it can save a game or destroy the opponent's plan at the decisive moment.
conclusion-joker.highlight: 🃏 The Joker embodies tactical versatility: one card, five uses, a thousand possibilities. Mastering its timing is mastering UNIT!

rules.title: Game Rules
rules.subtitle: Discover all the rules and become a master of UNIT. Click on a card to learn more.

general.title: General Rules
general.description: The basics of the game and fundamental principles
rules: The game is played with a standard 52-card deck plus 2 jokers
The goal is to create columns of cards following specific rules
Special cards have unique powers that can change the course of the game
strategies: Always keep a special card in reserve
Observe your opponents' game
Plan your actions several moves ahead

faq.question: How many cards can you have in hand?
faq.answer: Each player can have up to 5 cards in hand.

faq.question: Can you play multiple cards per turn?
faq.answer: No, only one card can be played per turn.

king.title: The King
king.description: Control the board with the King
rules: The King can be placed on any card
It allows you to take control of an entire column
Once placed, the King can only be moved by another King
strategies: Use the King to capture strategic columns
Keep a King in reserve to counter your opponent's
Combine the King with other special cards for powerful combos

faq.question: Can a King be moved?
faq.answer: Yes, but only by another King.

faq.question: Can you have multiple Kings in the same column?
faq.answer: No, only one King can control a column at a time.

queen.title: The Queen
queen.description: Use the power of the Queen
rules: The Queen can move freely on the board
She can take any card except a King
The Queen can protect adjacent cards
strategies: Use the Queen to protect your important cards
Create synergies with other special cards
Place the Queen strategically to block opponent moves

faq.question: Can the Queen take a King?
faq.answer: No, the King is the only card that the Queen cannot take.

jack.title: The Jack
jack.description: Master the movements of the Jack
rules: The Jack allows you to move a card to another column
It can be used to reorganize the playing field
Cannot move Kings
strategies: Use the Jack to disrupt opponent strategies
Move key cards to create opportunities
Save your important cards from dangerous situations

faq.question: Can the Jack move multiple cards at once?
faq.answer: No, the Jack can only move one card at a time.

joker.title: The Joker
joker.description: Discover the special powers of the Joker
rules: The Joker can copy the power of any card
It can be played at any time
Only one Joker can be active at a time
strategies: Save the Joker for critical situations
Adapt your strategy based on available powers
Use the Joker to surprise your opponents

faq.question: Can the Joker copy a King?
faq.answer: Yes, the Joker can copy any card, including the King.

lucky7.title: Lucky 7
rules: The 7 allows you to draw an additional card
If you draw another 7, you can draw again
Maximum of three cards can be drawn per turn
strategies: Use the 7 when you need specific cards
Combine with other cards for powerful combos
Keep a 7 in reserve for critical moments

faq.question: Can you play the drawn cards immediately?
faq.answer: No, drawn cards can only be played on the next turn.

units.title: The Units
units.description: Learn to use the basic cards
rules: Units are cards from 2 to 10
They can be placed in any column
Units follow specific placement rules
strategies: Create combinations with special cards
Use units to prepare for bigger moves
Don't underestimate the power of small units

faq.question: How do you place units?
faq.answer: Units must be placed according to their value and color.
